title: Mini handoff + interview notes — Ryan Wu
content:
Quick scratchpad to hand off Ryan Wu to the hiring panel — rough, unpolished. Notes to self and suggestions for next steps.

Candidate snapshot:
- Role: Senior Inference Engineer (runtime/optimization)
- Location: Remote (PST overlap)
- Recruiter screen: 2026-02-18 (me)
- Phone tech screen: 2026-02-25 (Marcus)
- Take-home suggestion: optional micro-bench + perf writeup (see linked GH example)

High-level impression:
- Very strong systems background: low-level performance tuning, familiarity with CUDA and Triton patterns, has implemented attention kernel optimizations at a previous company.
- Practical benchmarking experience: writes reproducible perf harnesses, aware of noise control and warmup nuances.
- Knows quantization tradeoffs (PTQ/QLoRA familiarity) and had hands-on with int8 kernels.

Concrete strengths observed:
- Depth on kernel-level improvements: specific example about rearranging memory layout to reduce L2 thrash (gave pseudocode).
- Good debugging instincts: uses metrics-first approach (latency histograms, CPU/GPU utilization, memcpy hotspots).
- Communication: concise, uses diagrams when explaining pipeline stages.

Areas to probe more (open questions):
- Service-level design: how would they design a multi-tenant GPU pool with graceful degradation? Need to see routing/fallback thinking.
- Orchestration familiarity: experience with autoscaling policies beyond simple up/down (e.g., batching-aware scale-to-zero).
- Ownership across infra/product: past scope seems IC+lead, but unclear on hiring/mentoring experience.

Red flags / concerns:
- Slightly narrow product POV — tends to optimize for microbenchmarks; ensure they can balance product constraints (SLOs, cost).
- Compensation expectation was a little above our midband; confirm alignment before looping VP of Eng.

Scoring draft (subjective) — scale 1–5 per category:
- Technical depth (low-level): 5
- Systems architecture: 3
- Communication & team fit: 4
- Shipping/operational experience: 3
- Overall: 15/20 (~7.5/10)

Suggested interview plan / next steps:
1) Loop in one senior SRE/Platform engineer for a 45m architecture deep dive: focus on multi-tenant routing, fallback policies, and KV cache management.
2) Pairing session (60m) on a small optimization task — e.g., reduce latency variance in a mocked serving loop; judge approach rather than finish.
3) Check references specific to shipped infra changes (ask for before/after perf reports).
4) Confirm comp band with Recruiting and hiring manager before scheduling final round.

To hand off to Marcus/Aisha:
- Read the phone notes (attached in Confluence link).
- If Agree to interview plan, coordinate calendar for SRE pairing next week.
- If concerns about product fit remain, consider adding a product-manager stakeholder to the loop.

Open TODOs for me:
- Draft an internal email intro for the panel (include perf harness link and GH PR example).
- Capture salary boundary and approval thread.

Misc scratch ideas (notes-to-self):
- If we progress: propose a custom mini-assignment that mirrors Redwood's KB caching challenge (short, 4–6 hours).
- Save example perf harness in GH under hiring-scripts for reuse.

End of draft — mark for follow-up after Marcus's notes come in.
